items.stem: An agile project within PRINCE2 has a fixed launch date and budget but cannot complete every requested feature. The recommended approach is to:

options.text: Flex scope by delivering the highest-priority requirements first
options.rationale: Correct: in this blend, time and cost are fixed and scope flexes by priority.
The date is fixed in this scenario.

options.text: Cut quality to fit everything in
options.rationale: Quality is protected, not sacrificed, when flexing scope.
A prioritised release can still deliver value.

items.explanation: Correct: in this blend, time and cost are fixed and scope flexes by priority.

items.stem: Marking nearly every requirement as 'Must have' in MoSCoW undermines prioritisation because it:

options.text: Removes the flexibility needed to protect the fixed deadline
options.rationale: Correct: too many 'musts' leaves no scope to flex, defeating the technique.
It is a design flaw, not illegal.
It does the opposite by overcommitting.

options.text: PRINCE2 governance and principles are retained, not discarded
options.rationale: Correct: the blend keeps PRINCE2 governance while working in an agile way.

options.text: Delivery is tailored to use agile practices and cadence
options.rationale: Correct: agile practices are tailored into the project.
Management stages remain in the blend.
Governance roles such as the project board remain.
